overview: Cross-sectional survey of adults within their first six months of systemic cancer therapy at four day units over three months, with a checkbox agreement analysis.
population: Consecutive adults within six months of starting systemic therapy attending on sampled clinic days from February to April 2027; one questionnaire per person.
exposure: Age, household income, employment change, travel distance, therapy type and benefits status; for the second question, the financial problems checkbox on the distress screening form.
procedures: The coordinator samples clinic days at random, approaches every eligible patient, records age, sex, postcode and months since starting treatment for everyone approached, and offers three modes in four languages; the distress screening form closest in time within four weeks is linked by the clinical team.

outcomes.name: Moderate or severe financial toxicity
outcomes.measure: Score in the moderate or severe range on the validated 11-item questionnaire
outcomes.why: The prevalence leadership needs, in the months when spending peaks.

outcomes.name: Checkbox agreement
outcomes.measure: Proportion of patients with moderate or severe financial toxicity who ticked the checkbox, and kappa
outcomes.timing: Checkbox within four weeks of the questionnaire
outcomes.why: Whether current screening finds affected patients (claim c2).

outcomes.name: Out-of-pocket spending
outcomes.measure: Self-reported spending on travel, parking and medicines in the previous month

outcomes.name: Response by group
outcomes.measure: Completed questionnaires divided by patients approached, by age, language and distance
outcomes.why: Non-response hides the most affected (claim c3).

feasibility: About 900 eligible attenders within six months of starting treatment in three months.
biasMitigation: Checkbox linked by staff not involved in scoring

biasFlags.label: Non-response among the most affected
biasFlags.note: Weighted estimates reported alongside crude ones.

parsimony.simplestPath: One questionnaire, one primary outcome, one agreement analysis.

summary: Revised survey restricted to the first six months of treatment with a checkbox agreement analysis.
